synthesis: The source uses uniformly controlled shifted moment families as an intermediate representation: polynomial differential operators specialize those families to the target mollified V-moments, while symmetry-aware recombination and divided-difference integrals make the shifted kernels regular enough for that transfer at coincident shifts.
source_support: Unit u07 defines the three shifted families and states uniform asymptotics for shifts of size O(L^-1). Unit u08 applies Q(-L^-1 d/dshift) at the specified shift values and uses holomorphy plus Cauchy contours of radius comparable to L^-1 to preserve the uniform error when recovering the target constants. Units u11 and u15 combine three companion terms, align them by dummy-variable symmetries, and apply the divided-difference identity twice to remove apparent shift denominators; u17 performs the analogous six-term permutation recombination and regularization for the diagonal family.
nonparaphrase_operation: Connects two source-separated transformations into one mechanism: symmetry and divided differences first convert singular-looking companion expansions into regular uniform shifted formulas, and Cauchy-controlled polynomial differentiation then converts those formulas into mollified derivative-moment constants.
limits: The differential transfer requires holomorphy on the relevant O(L^-1) contours and error estimates uniform there, in addition to the distinct length and polynomial-vanishing hypotheses of Lemmas 3.1-3.3. The pole cancellations depend on the exact companion terms, kernel symmetries, and permitted variable swaps, so they do not establish a general cancellation rule; dense extracted formulas, especially in u15 and u17, require scan-aware verification before exact reuse.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct parents jointly establish a concrete representational pipeline unavailable from any one unit alone: u07-u08 supply the uniform shifted-to-V derivative interface, whereas u11, u15, and u17 establish how the source-specific shifted formulas cancel their apparent singularities. The synthesis preserves the analytic hypotheses, family-specific proof burden, and formula-extraction risk without treating the displayed shifted lemmas as proved by the interface itself.
